text.p: President Jacques Chirac, in a clear attack on the Socialist-led government, criticised on Monday moves to relax immigration laws, saying to do so would encourage more illegal immigration.

"It would be an encouragement (to illegal immigrants). The employment and social situation does not allow our country to do this...and it would feed those xenophobic and racist reactions which I hate," Chirac said in a live Bastille Day television interview.

Chirac was commenting on Socialist government plans to legalise up to 40,000 immigrants, many of them black Africans, who have been in legal limbo since the previous centre-right governments passed more restrictive legislation. Some have overstayed visas or cannot be expelled because they have children born in France and entitled to citizenship.

Chirac's comments following years of controversy over immigration which have fuelled the electoral rise of the Jean-Marie Le Pen's extreme-rightist National Front party which Chirac vowed in the interview to fight.
"One should not listen solely to one's heart. One should also use one's head and try and see where our nation's interest lies," the president said.

He said millions of legal foreign residents were mostly opposed to allowing open-door immigration because "they are terrified at the rejection it would provoke, from which they would be first to suffer".
